issue: kernel-support hard constraint conflicts with the pre-registration
definition: kernel_support = geom_frac * airy_frac, where geom_frac is the fraction of traced ray weight that lands inside the finite PSF window (half-width = ceil(max|du|,|dv|) + airy_radius_margin*airy_radius + 1, capped at max_half_px=40) and airy_frac is the Airy encircled-energy fraction inside that same window. It is evaluated on the nominal unit at the constraint-probe distances 100/200/300 mm, medium condition.
reason: under HC3 as registered (>= 0.999) none of the three frozen designs is feasible: 100% of the 42000 recorded rows per candidate sit below 0.999, and the constraint probe at 100/200/300 mm gives 0.973-0.987. The executed optimisation used 0.950, which every candidate passes. The gap is therefore a real deviation from the pre-registration, not a rounding difference.
scientific_reading: The 0.999 value is a *truncation* requirement on a finite PSF window. With max_half_px=40 and the Airy margin rule, the window is sized from the geometric footprint, and any residual Airy encircled-energy outside the window counts as lost. For this singlet at f/6.7-f/10 the Airy radius is ~1.4 px while the geometric footprint is 3-9 um, so the window is tight and 0.97-0.99 is the structural ceiling. 0.999 is unreachable for this optical model, which makes HC3 an ill-posed constraint rather than a strict one. That reading is *evidence for an amendment*, not a retroactive justification: the registered text is still what it is.
required_disclosure: every G3 surface shows 0.950 (as-run) next to 0.999 (pre-registered)
